summary: I judge all seven T2-01 acceptance criteria PASS from direct evidence. All three story checks ran and passed: pytest gave 65 passed, mypy was clean, and make check passed ruff check, ruff format and mypy. The diff stays inside the story's files list (pyproject.toml, uv.lock, polarimetry.py and one test file) and adds only numpy. I found no zero-for-missing coercion, mock data or config/run.yaml change. One criterion rests partly on inspection: the git log call for the failing-tests-first order was denied, so I could not confirm that order myself.

checks.criterion: Check: uv run mypy pipeline/src pipeline/tests
checks.evidence: Success: no issues found in 5 source files
ruff check passed, ruff format --check passed (6 files already formatted), mypy found no issues in 6 source files

checks.criterion: numpy added to pipeline/pyproject.toml, uv.lock updated, no other dependency, mypy --strict passes
checks.evidence: The diff adds only "numpy>=2.5,<3" to pyproject.toml and the matching entries to uv.lock. mypy was clean. The mypy strict setting is assumed to be in the repo config; I did not read it.

checks.criterion: ObsState has exactly three states and InvalidReason has string codes. Every function returns values with state and reason arrays, and NaN never means zero
checks.evidence: polarimetry.py:42-83 defines ObsState as MISSING, INVALID and VALID and InvalidReason as a StrEnum. StatedArray.__post_init__ (lines 117-148) rejects NaN for a VALID element and a number for a non-VALID element, and ties reason to state. The tests at test_polarimetry_decode.py:57-123 cover these rules.

checks.criterion: Failing tests were written first, with the F8, F9 and F10 cases at rtol=1e-10 and atol=1e-12
checks.evidence: test_polarimetry_decode.py:184-198 checks F8 (-43 dB and 5.011872336272722e-5). Lines 317-323 check F9 (0.01, and not 0.1). Lines 425-428 check F10 (60 degrees). Commit 670def0 is titled 'add failing tests', before the feat commit 9fe9daa. The git log call that would show the failing run was denied, so I confirmed the order only from commit order and titles.

checks.criterion: Zero DN and nodata give INVALID or MISSING with reasons; x_power is DENOMINATOR_INVALID for HH zero, nodata or noise with no epsilon; averaging test on DN 100 and 300
checks.evidence: Zero DN gives INVALID/DN_ZERO and nodata gives MISSING/NODATA (test lines 249-263, polarimetry.py:221-243). x_power tests are at lines 334-362. Line 236 checks that the mean of decoded power (50000k) differs from the power of the mean DN (40000k). Line 225 checks the function signatures.

checks.criterion: Angle conversion needs an explicit declared unit, raises otherwise, and converts to degrees
checks.evidence: polarimetry.py:368-384 raises ValueError for any unit other than 'radians' or 'degrees', including None. Tests at lines 436-456 cover 1.0 radians versus 1.0 degrees, units not inferred from magnitude, and the None and invalid-unit raises.

checks.criterion: Hypothesis property tests for monotonicity and db/linear agreement
checks.evidence: test_polarimetry_decode.py:476-492 uses @given. The monotone test asserts a strictly positive diff, and the agreement test uses the PRD tolerance.

checks.criterion: Nodata and the 83 dB offset are named constants or arguments with the PRD 7 formula cited
checks.evidence: PALSAR2_CALIBRATION_OFFSET_DB = 83.0 at polarimetry.py:214. nodata and calibration_offset_db are keyword arguments. The docstrings cite PRD 7 and F8.

findings.claim: x_power's docstring says the calibration offset cancels only under a shared-calibration assumption, but the code has no check for it.
findings.evidence: The ratio is computed as (hv/hh)**2 with no offset argument. This matches F9, so it is an optional note only.

resolution.reason: PRD 7 Decoding rules define x_power = (DN_HV / DN_HH)**2 for one product, the PALSAR-2 yearly mosaic, with a single stated offset (83 dB) for both channels, and say: "The ratio assumes both channels share the stated calibration and pass quality and noise checks." The offset cancels in the ratio, so it is not an input. x_power receives DN only, with no per-channel calibration metadata to compare, so a check here would mean inventing a calibration argument that PRD 7 and 8.11 do not define. The quality and noise half of the assumption is enforced: hh_noise_dominated and hv_noise_dominated are required arguments. Shared calibration is a property of the product record (PRD 8.11 ProductRecord.calibration_type) and belongs to product qualification on ingest, which is not built yet; meanwhile the docstring (polarimetry.py x_power) states that the function is valid only under that assumption. The reviewer also judged it optional and consistent with F9.

findings.claim: The failing-tests-first requirement could not be re-verified from a recorded failing run.
findings.evidence: I saw only the commit order and titles. The git log call was denied.

resolution.reason: The failing run is reproducible. git ls-tree 670def0 pipeline/src/terraluna_pipeline/ lists only __init__.py, py.typed and schema.py, so the tests were committed before polarimetry.py existed (it first appears in 9fe9daa). Rerunning that commit against its own tree, with git archive 670def0 pipeline extracted to a temp dir and PYTHONPATH=<tmp>/pipeline/src uv run pytest <tmp>/pipeline/tests/test_polarimetry_decode.py -p no:cacheprovider, gives "E ModuleNotFoundError: No module named terraluna_pipeline.polarimetry" at test_polarimetry_decode.py:20, "1 error during collection", exit 2. The progress log entry for T2-01 implement records the same failure. The masked-input regression tests in this round were also committed failing first (c77bbbb: 31 failed, 72 passed).
